summary.assessment: The run is reliable at the two ends of the set: it declined all five figures without data with a sensible reason and never produced values for a diagram, and it returned every number exactly where the figure prints it (B1 counts, B3 AUROCs, C5 pie percentages, A3 CI bounds) or where a simple bar or point sits on a clean axis (C1 within 0.3 % of the range). It fails on dense figures by returning a fraction of the data in a shape that cannot be keyed: 24 of 180 line points without x positions in B2, one number per item instead of 264 stacked segments in C3 (with 137-175 % on a 0-100 axis), and in the vector figure C4 correct geometry under hex-colour series names and truncated tick labels, with a box plot typed as a line and a legend swatch read as a bar. Measured marks without printed labels are approximately right but not precise: forest centres off by up to 0.10 on a 3.1 range (B4) and 4 of 30 box medians beyond 5 % (B5), and interval or whisker bounds are missing, collapsed or wrong in every figure that needs them measured. A recurring cosmetic defect is an axis range that drops the lowest tick (B1, B4, C3), which triggers false 'outside the axis range' warnings on correct values. Its numbers can be taken as they are for figures with printed values and for simple single-series bar panels; line traces, stacked bars, box plots and measured confidence intervals need another reader or a check.
